Should declawing cats be against the law?

There are two ways of declawing, I've heard of. One is the inhumane way that ruins the nerves and is a dick move. The other is like having your nails trimmed, so they grow back. I feel like people do the former as oppposed to the latter to save money, which is cruel.

Honestly, you're getting a damn cat. You know they have pointy things. If you can't handle that, don't get a cat. Get them a scratching post and that is all that is needed really.

I don't think nail trimming is technically "declawing" - though correct me if I'm wrong. I think declawing refers specifically to the altogether removal of the cat's claws from its paws (see here).

Otherwise, though, I totally agree. It's like tearing off a child's fingernails instead of trimming them - maybe even worse.

Yes, declawing is the same as cutting of a tail of a dog. It's inhuman and people should be ashamed if they do it. What's next, removing their fangs because they can bite someone? How would we feel if someone removed our fingernails.

I don't ever want to declaw any cats.

With that said, I think there are reasonable arguments against making it illegal:

  • It is not the same as chopping off below the last knuckle for a human
  • I don't think cats have the ability to feel anguish over missing body parts (if they can: remember that we chop off their testicles and that's considered humane)
  • If it comes down to a decision between a cat being abandoned or declawed, I think the cat would rather be declawed

Either way it doesn't matter to me. I've seen cats without claws, and those with. Both are equally contented. It's a cat. It is not a human being with passionate emotions. They do not have the same desires like us. The only real argument for being against declawing is that the cat cannot defend itself, but most cats stay indoors, and do not encounter situations where they must fight predators. That said I do not think either party in this debate is wrong. Those for and against have equal merit. I know wthat's not what people want to hear... They want to hear their own opinions (confirmation bias), but that's the way I see it. Since I'm in the minority I will probably be downvoated.

Yes. Declawing is not the same as nail trimming. It is painful and you are removing something essential to what makes a cat a cat. This is the reason there are direct correlations between cats being declawed and then biting people once it becomes their only defense. Many times cats will also act out after having it done by peeing all over instead of in their box. Both of these things lead to cats being surrendered by their owners and ultimately euthanized. It is pushed by vets purely for profit. For these reasons, it is illegal in most countries. Don't want things being chewed? Don't get a puppy. Don't want things being scratched? Don't get a cat.
